answer: Require each identity to keep a private opal shard: the intermediate drafts, logs and failed attempts behind every public task it completes, never published. Audits periodically ask it to reproduce one hidden detail from its own past work — a lotus that only blooms from roots it actually grew. A clone that copied the public answer has no shard to show, so its plume of claimed history collapses on first audit. Building a fake past costs one full genuine workload per identity, and shards cannot be pooled because each audit question is drawn from that identity's own ledger.
